build: PAL original, two-sided G64; level 1 load in play

comments.text: Entry of the level 4 file. Jumps to the main loop at $1E15, which runs the setup $5118 and then repeats from $1E18: the disabled check $655D (a lone RTS), the object scan $0F0F, the energy bar $7803, the countdown sprite $1D85 and its test $1E85, the banner step $771E, the score $78B7, the timer $944C and $94EC and the pause check $739B. The loop starts again at $1E15 after the continue screen, and ends through the screen wipe $93AB, the sound silence $B828 and a jump to the resident loader at $0407 (level done, or the space key while the cheat flag $0A11 is set) or at $0404 (game over).
Set to 1 by the NMI handler at $0A23; cleared by the setup $5118 and read by the main loop at $1E64.
6 zero bytes between nmi_flag and slot_frame ($0A2C-$0A31), no reader.
Sprite pointer value of each slot, 14 bytes ($0A32-$0A3F); written by $101C and $1C47 and by the behaviours, and copied by $6593 into the pointer tables.
Sprite colour of each slot, 14 bytes; written by $1C47 and the behaviours and copied to $D02A-$D02E by $6593.
1 when a slot's sprite is multicolour, 14 bytes; set by $1C47 and the behaviours, and copied into $D01C by $6593.
Animation counter of each slot, 14 bytes; counted and used to pick frames or steps by the behaviours $134D, $13EF, $14F2 and $1A00, and cleared by $73C2.
Walk phase of each slot, 14 bytes, which picks the frame from the tables read by $1C47; cleared by $101C when it hits.
Frames left in the current walk of each slot, 14 bytes; counted down by the walking behaviours $1691 and $18DB, which reload it with half a random byte when it runs out, and cleared by $73C2.
Hurt timer of each slot, 14 bytes: set to 10 by $101C, counted down by the walking behaviours $1691 and $18DB (which do nothing else while it runs) and cleared by $73C2.

State of each slot (14 bytes, of which the first 11 are used): 0 free, otherwise the type copied from $0AA2 by $0F0F; the state picks the behaviour in the table at $11F5. $101C sets 1 or 2 on a hit and $615B sets $10; the behaviours change it too (the walkers $1691 and $18DB to attack or turn, the attacks back to 1 or 2, $573B to $18, $57A6 to $17, $6222 at $627D), and $73C2 clears it. 7 is handled by $1C47.

Type and state of each of the 73 objects; 0 means no object, and the value is copied into the slot state $0A94 when the object takes a slot. Copied from $78F0 by $73C2; $615B sets $10, and the behaviours that change a slot's state write it here too ($1691, $18DB, $573B, $57A6, $6222).

Counter of each object, used by the behaviours as a timer, step or saved state; copied from $7939 by $73C2, cleared by $101C on a hit, and set by $615B to the slot's old state (the entry after the object, $0AEC, is set to $FE).
Flag of each object; copied from $7982 by $73C2 and used by the behaviours.
Energy of each object (hits it can take), counted down by $615B; copied from $79CB by $73C2.

Variant flag of each object, 0, 1 or 2 (entries $11 and $24 of the table hold 2); copied from $7A14 by $73C2 and read at 20 places by the hit test $101C and the behaviours $155E, $1691, $17A9, $18DB, $1C47, $5398, $553A, $5672 and $6222.
A second flag of each object; copied from $7A5D by $73C2, and $101C sets a non-zero one to 2 when the object is hit.

Left limit of the object's walk, low byte; copied from $7AA6 by $73C2 and read by $101C, $1691 and other behaviours. Other objects use it otherwise: $134D takes it as the top of its patrol, and the enemy shot $1295 as its direction, which the attacks $155E and $17A9 set two entries on ($0C5A).
Left limit of the object's walk, high byte; copied from $7AEF.
Right limit of the object's walk, low byte; copied from $7B38.
Right limit of the object's walk, high byte; copied from $7B81.
World X of each object, low byte; copied from $7BCA and kept up to date by the behaviours and by $101C (which also writes the entry after the hit object).
World X of each object, high byte; copied from $7C13.
World Y of each object, low byte; copied from $7C5C.
World Y of each object, high byte; copied from $7CA5.
The object each of the slots holds (14 bytes), set by $0F0F, cleared by $73C2 and read by $117E, $1C47 and the blocking tests $751B and $7584.
The slot each object holds, for the 73 objects; set by $0F0F and cleared by $73C2. $1C47 reads it one entry back ($0EAD,Y) for the slot of the previous object.
Scratch of $0F0F: the object's X minus the camera X, low byte.
Scratch of $0F0F: the object's X minus the camera X, high byte.
Scratch of $0F0F: the object's Y minus the camera Y, low byte.
Scratch of $0F0F: the object's Y minus the camera Y, high byte.
Target of the beq at $0F14 in scan_objects (an object of type 0): a short hop to $0F9D, which releases the object's slot if it holds one, because the branch cannot reach it.

Scans the 73 objects, last to first (X from $48), against the camera ($FB/$FC across, $FD/$FE down). An object with type $0AA2 of 0, or outside the window (from 26 pixels left of the camera to less than $015A right of it, and $14 to $D6 below the camera's top) is released: if it holds a slot, that slot's state $0A94 is cleared, its height $CD,X is set to $FE and the object's flag $0FC0 is cleared. An object inside the window that has no slot takes the first free slot of the 11 ($0A94 zero), which gets the object's X and Y in $79/$B1 and $95/$CD and its state from the type, and $0EA0 and $0EAE link slot and object; the whole scan ends if no slot is free. Called once per pass by the main loop at $1E1B.
Holds the object index saved by $0FA2: the immediate operand of the LDX at $0FB2.
1 for each object that holds a slot, 73 bytes; set and cleared by $0F0F and cleared by $73C2.
The last 9 entries (objects 64 to 72) of obj_active ($0FC0), after the memory-map edge at $1000.
Set to 1 by $101C when it lands a hit, which makes further calls of $101C return at once; cleared by the player state routines (for example at $5D23).
Set to 1 by $101C on a hit, with $101A; $615B reads it to take 2 instead of 1 from the object's energy.

For slot X (object Y), tests whether the player's punch or strike hits it. It returns at once when a hit was already scored and the player state routines have not yet cleared the flags ($101A or $101B set), when neither the punch timer $5B4C nor the strike timer $5ABE is running, or when the slot's state $0A94 is not 1, 2, 14 or 15; the slot's screen height $A3,X must be at most $17 lines above or 9 lines below the player's $1D81 and its screen X within 25 pixels in front of the player's $1D80, on the side given by the facing $594B. On a hit it pushes the object 9 pixels along the map in that direction unless it is already at its limit ($0CEA/$0D33 to the right, $0C58/$0CA1 to the left), copies the new X to the slot and to the next object too, sets the slot to state 1 (player facing right) or 2 (facing left) with a frame in $0A32 that depends on the variant $0BC6, starts the hurt timer $0A86 with 10, sets $101A and $101B and calls $615B. Called by $117E for each slot that is not in state 7, while the raster is above line $B4.
Number of state 7 slots queued in $1170 by $117E.
List of the slots in state 7 found by $117E (ended by $FF), handled after the others by $1C47; cleared by $73C2.

Object update, called by the top interrupt at $6510 on each frame that the banner flag $771A is zero, and skipped while the game is paused ($63EA). Goes through the 11 slots: a slot in state 7 is only queued in the list at $1170 (count in $116F); for the others, while the raster is above line $B4 (the loop stops for the rest of the slots once it is not), it runs the hit test $101C and then the behaviour for the slot's state, through the table at $11F5 and a call whose operand is rewritten at $11C9/$11CA, with the slot's object in Y and in $11F4. The list is ended with $FF and each queued slot then goes through $1C47.

Low byte of the address in the JSR at $11C8 (high byte at $11CA), rewritten by $11BC and $11C2 with the behaviour for the slot's state from the table at $11F5; the $122B the file holds is only a placeholder.
Holds the queue index saved by $11DF: the immediate operand of the LDX at $11ED.
The object of the slot being handled by $117E and $1C47 (the Y register for the hit test and the behaviours).

Table of the 27 behaviour routines, one word each, indexed by the slot state in $0A94: 0 $122B behave_free, 1 $1691 behave_walk_left, 2 $18DB behave_walk_right, 3 $1A00 behave_energy_pickup, 4 $1ABE behave_score_pickup, 5 $1B00 behave_flash_frame, 6 $1B20 behave_lobbed_shot, 7 $1C47 slot_follow, 8 $1D03 behave_none, 9 $14F2 behave_flashing_hazard, 10 $134D behave_vertical_patrol, 11 $13EF behave_radial_shot, 12 $1328 behave_colour_6, 13 $1333 behave_colour_1, 14 $17A9 behave_attack_right, 15 $155E behave_attack_left, 16 $6222 behave_knocked_down, 17 $1295 behave_enemy_shot, 18 $538F behave_none_18, 19 $5398 behave_path_follower, 20 $54B3 behave_fixed_sprite, 21 $553A behave_timed_blast, 22 $5672 behave_bouncer, 23 $573B behave_falling_object, 24 $57A6 behave_falling_burst, 25 $122C behave_countdown_start, 26 $1262 behave_countdown_light. $117E copies the word into the operand of the call at $11C8.
Behaviour for state 0 (entry 0 of the table at $11F5): a lone RTS, so a slot in state 0 does nothing.

Behaviour for state $19 (entry 25 of the table at $11F5), reached for the object of type $19 in the table at $78F0. While the countdown flag $5117 is zero it runs the contact test $52F5; on contact it sets $5117 to 1, the three countdown digits $1D82-$1D84 to 9, the banner flag $771A to 1 and the banner timer $771B to $C8. It always makes the slot multicolour ($0A4E) with colour 6 ($0A40) and sprite pointer $70 ($0A32).

Behaviour for state $1A (entry 26 of the table at $11F5), reached for the object of type $1A in the table at $78F0. Sets sprite pointer $60, colour 1 and a single-colour sprite. While the countdown flag $5117 is non-zero it counts the slot's phase $0A6A down from $0D to 0 (restarting at $0E) and takes the pointer $61 for phases 7 and up and $60 below, so the sprite changes shape every 7 frames.

Behaviour for state $11 (entry 17 of the table at $11F5): the shot of a walking enemy, the object two entries after the one that fires it. Makes the slot multicolour with colour $0B and pointer 0 (nothing to see). While the object's counter $0AEB is zero it only copies the X of the object two before it ($0D7A, $0DC3) to this object and to the slot. The attacks $155E and $17A9 set the counter to $32; the shot then counts it down, runs the contact test $52F5 (on contact it calls $5367 and clears the counter) and moves the slot 5 pixels a frame right with pointer $73, or left with pointer $74 when $0C58 of the object is non-zero (the attacks set $0C5A for it). It clears the counter when the slot has left the screen.
Behaviour for state 12 (entry 12 of the table at $11F5): only makes the slot multicolour ($0A4E) with colour 6 ($0A40); the pointer stays as it was. No object in the table at $78F0 has type 12.
Behaviour for state 13 (entry 13 of the table at $11F5): only makes the slot multicolour ($0A4E) with colour 1 ($0A40); the pointer stays as it was. No object in the table at $78F0 has type 13.
Sprite pointers of behaviour $134D: $68 seven times and $69 eight times, indexed by the slot's $0A5C (14 down to 0), so it shows $69 for eight steps and then $68 for seven.

Behaviour for state 10 (entry 10 of the table at $11F5). Makes the slot multicolour with colour 0, counts its $0A5C down from 14 to 0 (a value of $0F or more, or 0, restarts at $0F) and takes the pointer from the table $133E by it. It then moves the slot 2 lines a frame between two heights: with the object's counter $0AEB at 0 it goes up until its Y ($95/$CD) equals the pair $0C58/$0CA1 and sets the counter to 1; with the counter at 1 it goes down until Y equals $0CEA/$0D33 and sets it to 0. The new Y is written to $0E0E/$0E57. There is no contact test.
Holds the Y register saved by $136A: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1374.

The eight steps of behaviour $13EF, 4 bytes each (X change low and high, Y change low and high, 16-bit and signed), chosen by the slot's $0A5C: up (0,-4), up and right (4,-4), right (4,0), down and right (4,4), down (0,4), down and left (-4,4), left (-4,0), up and left (-4,-4).
The step that $13EF has chosen, copied from $13CB: X change low and high, Y change low and high, added to the slot's X ($79/$B1) and Y ($95/$CD).

Behaviour for state 11 (entry 11 of the table at $11F5). Makes the slot multicolour with colour $0B and pointer $67 and runs the contact test $52F5: on contact it calls $5367 and restarts at $145E. Otherwise, while the object's counter $0AEB is non-zero, it counts it down and adds one of eight steps to the slot's position (the table $13CB, chosen by the slot's $0A5C, copied to $13EB-$13EE). At $145E it sets the counter to $1E, steps $0A5C on (0 to 7), puts the slot at the position of the object before this one ($0D7B, $0DC4, $0E0D, $0E56) and plays sound effect 7 (X = $1C) through $B0EE. So it starts from the object before it every 31 frames and flies 4 pixels a frame for 30 of them in the next of eight directions.
Holds the Y register saved by $1416: the immediate operand of the LDY at $143D.
Holds the Y register saved by $1489: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1491.
Holds the X register saved by $1486: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1493.

The 90 sprite pointers of the flashing hazard of behaviour $14F2, indexed by the slot's counter $0A5C: $6F ten times, $6E ten times, $6D sixteen times, $6E three times and $6F three times (42 steps with a picture), then 48 zeros for which the behaviour skips the contact test. The two zero bytes after it ($14F0-$14F1) are not read.

Behaviour for state 9 (entry 9 of the table at $11F5). Makes the slot multicolour ($0A4E) with colour $0B ($0A40), counts its counter $0A5C down from $59 to 0 (a value of $5A or more, or 0, restarts it at $59) and takes the sprite pointer $0A32 from the table $1496 by that counter, so the hazard shows for 42 of every 90 steps. When the pointer is not zero it runs the contact test $52F5, and when that returns non-zero it calls $5367 to hurt the player. It does not move the slot.
Holds the Y register saved by $150F: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1519, which gives Y back after the table lookup.

Returns A=1 when slot X is at or to the right of the player on the screen (its screen X high byte $BF,X is non-zero, or its screen X $87,X is not below the player's $1D80) and A=0 when it is to the left. Called by the behaviours of states 1 and 2 ($1758, $19A1).

Returns A=0 when slot X is about level with the player and A=1 when it is not: the slot's screen height $A3,X is compared with the player's $1D81, and the answer is 0 when they are equal, when the slot is less than 10 lines above the player and when it is less than $1C lines below him. Called by the behaviours of states 1, 2, 14 and 15 ($15E5, $16C3, $1830, $190D).

Hit recoil counter, counted down by $62BF; while it is running (and $5365 is zero) the joystick bytes $1EC5/$1EC6 are not refreshed, so the direction that an attack forced stays. $5367 sets it to 3 and the attacks $155E and $17A9 (at $160B and $1855) to 4; the top interrupt $6428 keeps the player's sprites 0 and 1 white while it is non-zero.

Behaviour for state 15 (entry 15 of the table at $11F5): the attack of a walking enemy that faces left, entered from $1691 with the object's counter $0AEB at $19. It makes the slot multicolour and, by the variant $0BC6, writes the frames and distances into six operands of its own code ($15BD, $15C5, $15D4, $15DC, $1638, $164C; variant 1 in brackets). At counter 0 it returns to state 1. Counting down: at 4 frame 5 ($14) and 8 (6) pixels right; at $0E frame 7 ($17) and 6 pixels left, and if the player is level ($153C) and up to 27 pixels left of the slot it forces the joystick left ($1EC5), sets the recoil $155D to 4 and calls $5374; if the object's flag $0B34 is set it clears it and starts the shot two objects on (counter $32, X of the slot, direction $0C5A set to 1); at $12 it moves 2 (0) pixels left and sets the phase $0A6A to 2; at $18 it takes frame 5 ($16).
Frame (sprite pointer) that $155E gives the slot when its counter reaches 4: the operand of the LDA at $15BC, set to 5 or, for variant 1, $14 at $156A and $158B.
Distance in pixels that $155E moves the slot right when its counter reaches 4: the operand of the ADC at $15C4, set to 8 or, for variant 1, 6 at $156F and $1590.
Frame (sprite pointer) that $155E gives the slot when its counter reaches $0E: the operand of the LDA at $15D3, set to 7 or, for variant 1, $17 at $1574 and $1595.
Distance in pixels that $155E moves the slot left when its counter reaches $0E: the operand of the SBC at $15DB, set to 6 for both variants at $1579 and $159A.
Distance in pixels that $155E moves the slot left when its counter reaches $12: the operand of the SBC at $1637, set to 2 or, for variant 1, 0 at $157E and $159F.
Frame (sprite pointer) that $155E gives the slot when its counter reaches $18: the operand of the LDA at $164B, set to 5 or, for variant 1, $16 at $1583 and $15A4.
Sprite pointers of the walk to the left for variant 0: $05 eight times, $06 eight times, and the same again, indexed by the phase $0A6A (0 to $1F); read by behaviour $1691.
Sprite pointers of the walk to the left for variant 1: $14 eight times, $15 eight times, and the same again, indexed by the phase $0A6A (0 to $1F); read by behaviour $1691.

Behaviour for state 1 (entry 1 of the table at $11F5): an enemy walking left. Makes the slot multicolour with colour 0. When the object's second flag $0C0F is neither 0 nor 2 it only shows the standing frame $05 ($14 for variant 1). Otherwise, with $0A10 zero and the player level ($153C) and up to 26 pixels left of the slot, it starts the attack: state 15 with the counter $0AEB at $19. While the hurt timer $0A86 runs it only counts it down. If the object two on has type $11 and an idle counter ($0AED), the slot is on screen at a height of $64 to $BD and a random byte ($653D) is below $14, it sets the flag $0B34 and attacks too. At its left limit ($0C58/$0CA1) it turns to state 2 (slot and object type). When the walk counter $0A78 has run out it takes half a random byte and turns when the slot is left of the player ($152B); otherwise it moves 1 pixel left (X $79/$B1, also written to this object and the next) and steps the phase $0A6A through 0 to $1F, taking the frame from $1651 (variant 0) or $1671.

Behaviour for state 14 (entry 14 of the table at $11F5): the attack of a walking enemy that faces right, entered from $18DB with the object's counter $0AEB at $19. The same as $155E the other way round: it writes frames and distances into six operands of its own code ($1808, $1810, $181F, $1827, $1882, $1896; variant 1 in brackets) and at counter 0 returns to state 2. At 4 frame 2 ($10) and 8 (6) pixels left; at $0E frame 4 ($13) and 6 pixels right, and if the player is level and up to 27 pixels right of the slot it forces the joystick right, sets the recoil $155D to 4 and calls $5374; a set flag $0B34 starts the shot two objects on with direction 0; at $12 it moves 2 (0) pixels right and sets the phase $0A6A to 2; at $18 it takes frame 2 ($12).
Frame (sprite pointer) that $17A9 gives the slot when its counter reaches 4: the operand of the LDA at $1807, set to 2 or, for variant 1, $10 at $17B5 and $17D6.
Distance in pixels that $17A9 moves the slot left when its counter reaches 4: the operand of the SBC at $180F, set to 8 or, for variant 1, 6 at $17BA and $17DB.
Frame (sprite pointer) that $17A9 gives the slot when its counter reaches $0E: the operand of the LDA at $181E, set to 4 or, for variant 1, $13 at $17BF and $17E0.
Distance in pixels that $17A9 moves the slot right when its counter reaches $0E: the operand of the ADC at $1826, set to 6 for both variants at $17C4 and $17E5.
Distance in pixels that $17A9 moves the slot right when its counter reaches $12: the operand of the ADC at $1881, set to 2 or, for variant 1, 0 at $17C9 and $17EA.
Frame (sprite pointer) that $17A9 gives the slot when its counter reaches $18: the operand of the LDA at $1895, set to 2 or, for variant 1, $12 at $17CE and $17EF.
Sprite pointers of the walk to the right for variant 0: $02 eight times, $03 eight times, and the same again, indexed by the phase $0A6A (0 to $1F); read by behaviour $18DB.
Sprite pointers of the walk to the right for variant 1: $10 eight times, $11 eight times, and the same again, indexed by the phase $0A6A (0 to $1F); read by behaviour $18DB.

Behaviour for state 2 (entry 2 of the table at $11F5): an enemy walking right, the mirror of $1691. Makes the slot multicolour with colour 0; with the object's second flag $0C0F neither 0 nor 2 it only shows the standing frame $02 ($10 for variant 1). With $0A10 zero and the player level ($153C) and up to 26 pixels right of the slot it starts the attack: state 14 with the counter $0AEB at $19; the same random shot test as $1691 can start it too. At its right limit ($0CEA/$0D33) it turns to state 1. When the walk counter $0A78 has run out it takes half a random byte and turns when the slot is right of the player ($152B); otherwise it moves 1 pixel right and steps the phase $0A6A through 0 to $1F, taking the frame from $189B (variant 0) or $18BB.
Sprite pointers of behaviour $1A00: $62 seven times and $63 seven times, indexed by the slot's $0A5C (11 down to 0); the last two bytes are never read.

Behaviour for state 3 (entry 3 of the table at $11F5): a pickup that gives energy. Makes the slot multicolour with colour 2. When the object's energy $0B7D is non-zero (taken) the pointer is 0 and nothing else happens. Otherwise the pointer comes from $19F2 by the slot's $0A5C (11 down to 0) and the slot bobs: the object's counter $0AEB steps by 2 round the 24 heights of $1A8E, which are added to its Y and written to $0E0E/$0E57. On contact ($52F5) it sets the object's energy to 1, adds $18 to the player's energy $5366 (at most $21) and plays sound effect 4 (X = $10).
Holds the Y register saved by $1A2D: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1A37.
Holds the Y register saved by $1A81: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1A89.
Holds the X register saved by $1A7E: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1A8B.

The 24 heights of the bobbing of behaviour $1A00, signed 16-bit values added to the slot's Y each frame, chosen by the object's counter $0AEB (steps of 2): 0, 0, -1, -1, -2, -2, -3, -3, -2, -2, -1, -1 and the same with the opposite signs, so the pickup rises 18 lines and comes back.

Behaviour for state 4 (entry 4 of the table at $11F5): a pickup that gives points. Makes the slot multicolour with colour 3. When the object's energy $0B7D is non-zero (taken) the pointer is 0; otherwise it is $6C and the contact test $52F5 runs: on contact the object's energy becomes 1, 6 is added to score digit 4 through $788B (600 points, going by the digit positions described there) and sound effect 3 (X = $0C) plays.
Holds the X register saved by $1AE4: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1AEE.
Holds the Y register saved by $1AF3: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1AFB.
Holds the X register saved by $1AF0: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1AFD.

Behaviour for state 5 (entry 5 of the table at $11F5). Makes the slot multicolour with colour 9; while the object's counter $0AEB is non-zero it counts it down and shows pointer $6B, otherwise pointer $6A. This routine never sets the counter; in the object list the type 5 object stands directly before the type 6 object, whose behaviour $1B20 sets the counter of the object before it to 7 when it restarts.

Behaviour for state 6 (entry 6 of the table at $11F5). Makes the slot multicolour and runs the contact test $52F5: on contact it calls $5367 and restarts at $1B96. Otherwise colour 2 and pointer $67; the object's counter $0AEB, stepped each frame, runs through the table $1BDA: from 4 to $33 the slot moves 4 pixels left, and each table value of $5A or more is a sprite pointer while a smaller one is added to the slot's Y (written to the object too). At $6A, or on contact, $1B96 clears the counter, sets the counter of the object before it ($0AEA) to 7, puts the slot and the object $16 pixels left of and 1 line above that object and plays sound effect 5 (X = $14).
Holds the Y register saved by $1BCD: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1BD5.
Holds the X register saved by $1BCA: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1BD7.

106 bytes read by behaviour $1B20, indexed by its counter $0AEB after the step, and by $57A6 from $1C0E. A value of $5A or more is a sprite pointer, a smaller one a number of lines added to the slot's Y. Indexes 0 to 3: pointers $7B, $7C, $7B, $7C; 4 to 13: 0; 14 to 51: 0 to 5 lines, growing; 52 to 105: the burst frames $72 (6), $71 (6), $64 (5), $65 (5), $66 (5), $64 (5), $65 (5), $66 (5), $71 (6), $72 (6).
The frame limit that $1C47 compares the previous slot's frame with: 5, or $14 for variant $0BC6 non-zero.
One zero byte between follow_limit and follow_slot ($1C45), no reader.
The slot of the previous object, saved by $1C47 while it reads the object's variant.

Behaviour for a slot in state 7 (entry 7 of the table at $11F5), run by $117E after the other slots. Makes the slot multicolour ($0A4E) with colour 0 ($0A40) and copies the object's position ($0D7C/$0DC5) to the slot ($79/$B1). It then picks the sprite pointer $0A32 from the slot of the previous object ($0EAD,Y): from $61C8 or $6204 by that slot's phase $0A6A when it is in state $10, otherwise from $1CE3 when its frame is below the limit in $1C44 (5, or $14 for variant $0BC6 non-zero) and from $1CC3 when not. Probably the lower sprite of a two-sprite enemy that follows the upper one.
Frames $0C to $0F, eight each, indexed by the phase $0A6A of the previous slot: the sprite pointer $1C47 gives a state 7 slot when the previous slot's frame is not below the limit $1C44.

The level's main loop. It runs the setup $5118, then from $1E18 on every pass the disabled check $655D, the object scan $0F0F, the energy bar $7803, the countdown sprite $1D85 and test $1E85, the banner step $771E, the score $78B7, the timer $944C and its expiry $94EC and the pause check $739B. It then ends the level when $0A11 is set and the key code $9A80 is $20; when the energy $5366 is zero (and $0A11 is clear) it shows the game over screen $57FF and, when $0A12 is set, the continue screen $98A4, which sends the loop back to $1E15 if fire was pressed ($98A3); when the level-done flag $1EC1 is set it ends the level, and when the NMI flag $0A2B is set it shows the game over screen and leaves. It leaves through the screen wipe $93AB, SEI, the sound silence $B828 and a jump to the resident loader at $0407 (level done or space key) or $0404 (game over).
Low byte of the camera height $FD plus the player's screen height $1D81, worked out by $1E85.
High byte of the sum in $1E83, worked out by $1E85.

Returns at once when the countdown flag $5117 is zero. Set to 1 by $1E85 when the sum of camera and player height is $00FA to $00FF; the main loop at $1E5F then ends the level. Cleared by the setup.

It moves 2 pixels in the direction he faces ($594B; left through $751B, right through $7584): facing left, a blocker or the map's left end (map X below $0039) sends him 2 pixels right instead, while facing right a blocker or the map's right end stops him, and a solid tile puts his X back from $58B5; puts frame $9B or $A1 in $60BC and counts the strike timer $5ABE down with the strike frames ($5991), setting the strike delay $5ABD to 10 when it runs out.
Set to 10 by $59D0 and $5E30 when the strike timer $5ABE runs out and counted down by them while it is zero. Nothing else in the traced code reads it.
Frames left of the strike: set to $0E when a strike starts ($5AC3, $5B4E) and counted down by the strike $59D0 and the jump $5E30; the hit test $101C, $60C0 and $63EB read it.
Non-zero while the player is crouching, and through a strike begun from a crouch ($5AC3 does not clear it; the strike's end does). $60C0 and the contact test $52F5 read it.
Delay before the player can crouch or strike from state 1: set to 10 when a strike or a crouch ends, to 4 when a climb ends and to 0 when a jump ends; counted down by $5B4E.
Frames before the next punch can start: set to 6 when a punch ends ($5972) and counted down by $5B4E.
Delay before the next jump can start: set to 10 on every frame of a climb ($5F9F) and counted down by $5B4E, which starts a jump only when it is zero.

Player state 6, crouching (entry 6 of the table at $58A5). Fire ($1EC5 bit 4) starts a strike: state 7, index $5E2E cleared, strike timer $5ABE set to $0E, strike frames ($5991) and sound effect 0 through $B0EE. With down released it returns to state 1 with the crouch delay $5AC0 set to 10 and the crouch flag $5ABF cleared. While down is held, left and right turn him ($594B) unless the recoil $155D is running, and the crouch frames ($5B27) are set either way.
Holds the Y register saved by $5ADF: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5AE7.
Holds the X register saved by $5ADC: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5AE9.
Sets the three sprite pointers in $60BD, $60BE and $60BF for the crouch: $92, $B6, $C0 when the player faces right and $93, $B7, $C1 when he faces left. Called by $5AC3 and $5B4E.
Frames left of the punch: set to 9 by $5B4E when a punch starts and counted down by $5972; the hit test $101C, $60C0 and $63EB read it.
Read by $5B4E at $5C69 (a non-zero value stops a climb down from starting); nothing in the traced code writes it, and the file holds 0.

Player state 1, standing and walking (entry 1 of the table at $58A5). Counts down the jump delay $5AC2, clears the hit flags $101A/$101B and the strike timer $5ABE, then moves 2 pixels left or right from the joystick $1EC5 (bits 2 and 3): it sets the facing $594B, steps the walk animation ($5909, $592A) unless the recoil $155D runs, and is stopped by a blocker ($751B, $7584), by the ends of the map (map X $1D04/$1D05 below $0039 or from $03A5 on) and by a solid tile (the player's X is put back from $58B5). It then goes to state 2 when the tile below is not solid, and otherwise starts a climb (up held on a ladder tile $0F/$10, or down held with $0D/$0E below, state 4), a jump (up held, state 3, when $5AC2 is zero), a strike (down and fire, state 7) or a crouch (down, state 6) when the crouch delay $5AC0 is zero (otherwise it counts that down), a punch (fire, state 5, when $5AC1 is zero), or with the stick centred shows the standing frame ($5D0E).
Holds the Y register saved by $5CAB: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5CB3.
Holds the X register saved by $5CA8: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5CB5.
Holds the Y register saved by $5CEB: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5CF3.
Holds the X register saved by $5CE8: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5CF5.
Puts the standing frame in $60BC: $9A when the player faces right and $A0 when he faces left. Called by $5B4E and $5D21.

Player state 2, falling (entry 2 of the table at $58A5). Clears the hit flag $101A, moves left and right from the joystick as in state 1 (facing $594B, blockers $751B/$7584, map ends, solid tiles; no walk animation), then lowers him by 3 lines a frame (2 from line $82, none from line $97) and, when the tile below is solid, returns to state 1 with the standing frame ($5D0E); otherwise it shows the falling frame ($5DCD).
Puts the falling frame in $60BC: $F8 when the player faces right and $F9 when he faces left. Called by $5D21.

Table of the 39 height steps of the jump, two bytes each, read by $5E30 through the index $5E2E: from -4 at the start to +4 at the end. They are written as signed 16-bit values, but $5E30 adds only the first byte of each pair to the 8-bit height $1D81, so the second bytes are never read.
Index into the jump and strike height tables ($5DE0, $59B6), two bytes a step; cleared when a jump or a strike starts ($5B4E, $5AC3) and stepped by $5E30 and $59D0.
When non-zero, $60C0 draws the player as in this state instead of the state in $58A4; set to 1, 3, 6 or 0 by $5B4E and to 3 by $5E30, and cleared by $60C0 after use.

Player state 3, a jump (entry 3 of the table at $58A5). Adds the next step of the table at $5DE0 (indexed by $5E2E) to the player's height $1D81. When the table is used up, or from index $29 on when the tile below is solid, it returns to state 1 (draw override $5E2F set to 3, strike timer $5ABE and crouch delay $5AC0 cleared). It steers left and right from the joystick as in state 1 (facing $594B, blockers $751B/$7584, map ends, solid tiles), counts a running strike timer down with the strike frames ($5991), and shows the jump frame ($5F2F).
Puts the jump frame in $60BC: $D5 when the player faces right and $D6 when he faces left. Called by $5B4E and $5E30.
1 while the player climbs up and 0 while he climbs down; set by $5B4E and $5F9F and read by $5F9F at the end of a climb.
Twelve sprite pointer values of the climb upwards ($94 to $96), indexed by $58E3 in $5F5B.
Twelve sprite pointer values of the climb downwards ($94 to $96), indexed by $58E3 in $5F7C.
Advances the climb frame upwards: toggles $5908 and, on every other call, steps $58E3 through 12, and on every call puts the frame from the table at $5F43 in $60BC. Called by $5F9F.
Advances the climb frame downwards: toggles $5908 and, on every other call, steps $58E3 through 12, and on every call puts the frame from the table at $5F4F in $60BC. Called by $5F9F.
Low byte of the camera height $FD plus the player's screen height $1D81, worked out by $5F9F; it allows a climb upwards only from $00FA on.
High byte of the sum in $5F9D, worked out by $5F9F.

Player state 4, climbing (entry 4 of the table at $58A5). Works out the camera height plus the player's height into $5F9D/$5F9E, sets the jump delay $5AC2 to 10 and moves him 1 line up (up held, only when that sum is $00FA or more, frames from $5F5B, $5F42 set to 1) or 1 line down (down held, frames from $5F7C, $5F42 set to 0). While the tile below him is $0F, $10, $0D or $0E the climb goes on; otherwise it returns to state 1 with the crouch delay $5AC0 set to 4 and the standing frame ($9A right, $A0 left), and a climb that went up ends 2 lines lower.

Clears the sorted sprite list at $0010 (puts $FF at the place each of the 11 slots had last frame, kept in $02-$0C), then turns each slot's world position ($79/$B1 across, $95/$CD down) into a screen position by subtracting the camera ($FB-$FE): across into $87,X and $BF,X, and, only for a slot whose X is on the screen, down into $A3,X and $DB,X. A slot off the screen (X of $0150 or more, or height outside $23 to $C7) gets place 0; one on the screen goes to the first free place from its height / 2 in the list, and its place is kept in $02,X. Ends the list with $64 in $78. Called by the top interrupt at $6478, before the multiplexer $6593.

Sprite pointer value of the player's main frame, used by $60C0 except while the punch timer $5B4C, the crouch flag $5ABF or the strike timer $5ABE is set outside states 2 to 4, when it takes $60BD-$60BF instead.
Sprite pointer for the player's sprite 2 while he punches, strikes or crouches; read by $60C0.
Sprite pointer for the player's sprite 0 while he punches, strikes or crouches; read by $60C0.
Sprite pointer for the player's sprite 1 while he punches, strikes or crouches; read by $60C0.

Writes the player's three sprite pointers into both screens' tables ($CFF8-$CFFA and $CBF8-$CBFA). The state drawn is $58A4, or the value in $5E2F when that is non-zero (which it then clears). For states 2 and 3 sprite 2 gets $60BC and sprites 0 and 1 get that plus 2 and plus 4, for state 4 the pointers are $60BC (sprite 2), plus $24 (sprite 0) and plus $2E (sprite 1); while the punch timer $5B4C, the crouch flag $5ABF or the strike timer $5ABE is set they come from $60BD (sprite 2), $60BE (sprite 0) and $60BF (sprite 1), and otherwise sprite 0 gets $60BC, sprite 1 that plus $0D and sprite 2 that minus $17. Called by $58B7.

Called by the hit test $101C with X the slot and Y the object. Takes 2 (when $101B is set) or 1 from the object's energy $0B7D and adds 4 to the score digit 5 ($788B); both calls in $101C set $101B just before, so it always takes 2. When the energy is already zero it instead copies the slot's state to the object's counter $0AEB, sets the slot and the object to state $10, sets the next object's counter $0AEC to $FE and adds 8 to the score digit 5.
Holds the slot index saved by $617D: the immediate operand of the LDX at $6187.
Holds the slot index saved by $619D: the immediate operand of the LDX at $61A7.

Sprite pointers of behaviour $6222 for variant 0, indexed by the phase $0A6A (0 to $1D): $18 ten times, then 20 zeros (no picture). Variant 1 reads the 30 bytes from $61E6 instead: $1C ten times (the end of follow_frames_a) and the zeros of knocked_frames_1_tail.

Sprite pointers $19, $1A, $1B and $1C, ten each, indexed by the phase $0A6A of the previous slot: the frame $1C47 gives a state 7 slot of variant 0 when the previous slot is in state $10. The extent is the run of the pattern.
The last 20 entries (all zero, no picture) of the variant 1 table of behaviour $6222, which starts at $61E6 with the ten $1C that end follow_frames_a ($61C8).
Sprite pointers $19, $1D and $1E, ten each, indexed by the phase: the frame $1C47 gives a state 7 slot of variant 1 when the previous slot is in state $10. It ends where the code at $6222 begins.

Behaviour for state $10 (entry 16 of the table at $11F5), which $615B gives an enemy whose energy has run out. Colour 0, multicolour. The phase $0A6A (which the hit test $101C has just cleared) steps with the counter of the next object ($0AEC, which $615B sets to $FE): at $1E or more it counts up to $1D, below that down to 0. The pointer comes from $61E6 (variant 1) or $61AA by the phase, after the step: the phase reaches 1 on the first update, so entries 1 to 9 show the shape and then 0, and the enemy shows for nine updates and disappears.

No caller: nothing calls, jumps to or points at it. Sets the object's energy $0B7D to 3 and gives slot and object the state that $615B saved in the counter $0AEB (1 or 2, the state $101C set just before; a value of 3 or more would have $0D taken off), then the walking pointer for it: 5 ($14 for variant 1) for state 1 and 2 ($10) for state 2. It would turn a knocked-down enemy back into a walking one.
Sets the screen matrix bits of $D018 to $30 (screen at $CC00) when $1EC8 is zero and to $20 ($C800) when it is not, keeping the other bits. Called by the top interrupt at $6451.

Raster interrupt 2 of 3 (vector $62BF), on line $C5 (set by $6428). Saves A, X and Y in the operands at $6387, $6389 and $638B, moves sprites 3-7 to line $0A, clears all sprite pointers $CFF8-$CFFF and $CBF8-$CBFF, turns the sprites off, writes $D018 for screen $CC00 and ORs $4F into $D011 for the panel, and acknowledges the interrupt. It counts down $5365 and the recoil $155D, and reads $DC00 (joystick port 2) into $1EC5 and $DC01 (port 1 and the keyboard) into $1EC6 unless the recoil is still running while $5365 is zero, sets the character set bits of $D018 to 8, runs the timer $948A and toggles $638E (counting $638D down on every second frame). It sets line $CD and the vector $638F for the next interrupt.
Holds the interrupted program's A register, stored by $62BF on entry: the immediate operand of the LDA at $6386.
Holds the interrupted program's X register, stored by $62C2 on entry: the immediate operand of the LDX at $6388.
Holds the interrupted program's Y register, stored by $62C5 on entry: the immediate operand of the LDY at $638A.
Counted down on every second frame by $62BF while it is not zero; nothing else in the traced code reads it.
Toggled every frame by $62BF.

Raster interrupt 3 of 3 (vector $638F), on line $CD (set by $62BF). Saves A, X and Y in the operands at $63E4, $63E6 and $63E8, ORs $17 into $D016 and writes it at once, then after 18 NOPs writes $D011 with $2F ORed in and $D016 again, which switches the status panel on (bitmap mode, multicolour), acknowledges the interrupt, sets raster line 1 and the vector $6428, clears bit 6 of $D011 and calls the scroll step $1ECD unless the banner flag $771A is set. It then restores A, X and Y and returns.
1 while the game is paused ($739B); the interrupts and routines skip the moving parts while it is set. Also set by the wipe $93AB.

Moves sprite 0 ($D000) by 8 pixels along X while the punch timer $5B4C runs, or sprite 1 ($D002) while the strike timer $5ABE runs, to the right when the player faces right ($594B zero) and to the left otherwise; does nothing when neither timer runs. Called by the top interrupt at $64E4.
0 during the first multiplexer pass of a frame and 1 during the second; cleared and then incremented by the top interrupt $6428 and read by $6593.

Raster interrupt 1 of 3 (vector $6428), on line 1 (set by $638F). Saves A, X and Y in the operands at $652E, $6530 and $6532, sets the fine scroll from $1EC2 ($D016) and $1EC3 ($D011), $D018 to $34, the screen ($62A9) and the multicolours. With the banner flag $771A set it calls $75EE and leaves. Otherwise it sorts the sprites ($6038), sets sprite 3 up as the countdown (pointer $FE, X $12F, Y $3B), turns the sprites on unless the wipe flag $93A9 is set, runs the first multiplexer pass ($6593, limit $29), the player ($58B7), the player's sprite positions (X $1D80, Y $1D81) and $63EB, and plays the sound ($B176). Sprites 0 and 1 are white while the recoil $155D is non-zero. A second pass ($6593, limit $8C), $6A61, the object update $117E and $7441 follow, then line $C5 and the vector $62BF.

Busy-wait: the outer count is A and the inner count is A as well (X and Y both start from A), so the callers' values from $14 to $FF give delays from a few milliseconds to about a third of a second. Used by the wipe, the game over, continue and briefing screens.

Returns a pseudo-random byte in A. It stores the low three bits of CIA 1 timer A ($DC04) as the offset of the branch at $654D, adds the timer's high byte ($DC05) to the seed $655C, and rotates the sum left through the carry (set) by a number of places from 2 to 9 that the patched branch picks. The result is the new seed and the return value. Called by the behaviours at $171D and $1966, which compare it with $14, and at $1751 and $199A, which halve it into the walk length $0A78.

The offset of the BCS at $654D, rewritten by $653D (at $6542) with the low three bits of $DC04, so that the branch lands between $654F and $6556 in the chain of ROL instructions up to $6557. The listing holds $01, left by the last call before the snapshot.
The seed of $653D: replaced by each result. The listing holds $95, left by the last call before the snapshot.
Starts with RTS, so it returns at once; the bytes after it are unused_check ($655E), which nothing reaches while the RTS is there. Called once per pass by the main loop at $1E18.

Reads $DD00 (CIA 2 port A) and returns when bit 2 is set. When it is clear it removes three bytes from the stack (three PLA), disables interrupts and jumps to $0810. Nothing reaches it: the main loop calls $655D, which is an RTS.
Fills the 1 KB screen matrix at $CC00-$CFFF with A. Called by the setup, the game over, continue and briefing screens.
Fills colour RAM $D800-$DBFF with A. Called by the game over, continue and briefing screens.
Index into the sprite list at $0010 of the last slot the multiplexer handled; set to $10 by the top interrupt before each frame's first pass.
Raster line limit for the multiplexer: $29 for the first pass, $8C for the second.

Sprite multiplexer for sprites 3 to 7, called twice a frame by the top interrupt $6428 (with the raster limit $29 and then $8C in $6592), and not at all while the banner flag $771A is set. Takes the next entry of the sorted sprite list at $0010 (position kept in $6591, $64 ends the list) and, while the raster line is below the limit, gives it the next of the five sprites whose previous slot has finished (its height $15 or more lines above the raster): height into $D007, $D009, $D00B, $D00D or $D00F, X into $D006, $D008, $D00A, $D00C or $D00E with its ninth bit in $D010, the pointer $0A32 into both screens' tables ($CFFB-$CFFF and $CBFB-$CBFF), the colour $0A40 and the multicolour bit $0A4E. On the first pass ($6427 zero) sprite 3 is left out and the order starts with sprite 4.

Bit masks for sprites 2 to 7 ($04, $08, $10, $20, $40, $80) followed by their complements ($FB, $F7, $EF, $DF, $BF, $7F). No code reads them: the multiplexer $6593 and the interrupts use immediate masks.
Set when the lower colours are to be copied from the buffer $712F: set to 1 by $679D, read and cleared by $6A61, and cleared by the setup at $517E.

Copies the colour buffer's rows 10 to 12 ($70B7-$712D, 39 colours of each row of 40) to colour RAM from $D990, and sets the flag $679C so that the interrupt copies rows 13 to 18 ($6A61). Called by the finish phase of every scroll ($202C, $258B, $2924 and others).

When the flag $679C is set, clears it and copies the colour buffer $712F-$721D to colour RAM $DA08-$DAF6 (screen rows 13 to 18, 39 characters in each, leaving out the last column of each row); otherwise returns at once. Called by the top interrupt at $650D on every frame except while the banner flag $771A is set.
Last part of the copy of the colour buffer $712F-$721D to colour RAM: screen rows 17 and 18, 39 colours each from $71CF and $71F7 to $DAA8 and $DAD0, ending with the RTS at $6FE8.

No caller: nothing calls or jumps to it. Jumps to colour_buffer_from_cc ($3867) when the buffer flag $1EC8 is non-zero and to colour_buffer_from_c8 ($44BF) when it is zero; the phase 2 routines of the scrolls make the same choice themselves.

Fills colour RAM rows 0 to 9 ($D800-$D98F) from the matrix just made: for each column Y from $28 down to 0 and each of the 10 rows it looks up the colour of the character in the colour table $BF00 (Y = $28 reaches column 0 of the next row, so $D990 is written too). It reads $C800 when the buffer flag $1EC8 is 0 and $CC00 when it is 1. Called by the finish phase of every scroll ($2029, $2588, $2921 and others).

Colours for screen rows 10 to 12, 40 bytes a row (120 bytes), built from the screen matrix by $3867 and $44BF (columns 0 to 38 of each row; the last byte of each row is never written) and copied to colour RAM from $D990 by $679D. Rows 13 to 18 follow at $712F.
Colours for screen rows 13 to 18, 40 bytes a row, one for each character; $6A61 copies 39 of each 40 to colour RAM from $DA08. The extent is what $6A61 reads.

Table of 77 16-bit pointers to the map rows, the first one twice: entry k from 1 on is $7CEE + 64 x (k - 1). It starts on an odd address because $1D06 reads the low byte from $7297,X and the high byte from $7298,X with X twice the map row. The last four rows (72 to 75, ending at $8FAE) point at $8EEE on, which holds the paths and not map rows.
Six bytes after the last row pointer: 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 4. No code reads them.

Draws the opening view: 10 rows of tiles from the map at $7E58 (64 bytes a row) into the screen at $CC00, each row as the right half of its first tile ($74E9) and 19 whole tiles ($74AB), with the bottom half left out for the tenth row. It then sets the colour RAM at $D800-$DAFF from the colour table at $BF00 indexed by each character. Called once by the setup $5118.
Pause: when the key code in $9A80 is $50, sets the paused flag $63EA, waits for the key to be released, pressed again and released, then clears $63EA. Called by the main loop at $1E33.

Copies the 73 entries of the 14 object tables from the level data at $78F0-$7CED into the working tables $0AA2-$0E9F (type, counter, flag, energy, variant, second flag, left and right limits, X and Y), clears the slot links $0EAE and the active flags $0FC0, and zeroes the 14-byte slot tables $0A5C, $0A78, $0A86, $0A94, $0EA0 and $1170. Called once by the setup $5118.

Counts the three-digit countdown $1D82-$1D84 (units first) down by one every seventh frame, using the delay $1E14 that it reloads with 6. Does nothing while the game is paused ($63EA); when the flag $5117 is zero it clears the three digits instead, and when all three are zero it returns. Called by the top interrupt at $6513.
The tile row number (0 to 9) that $7337 passes in X; $74AB and $74E9 keep it here and leave the bottom half of the tile out when it is 9.

Writes tile A as two by two characters at the screen pointer $ED/$EE: the top pair from the table at $90BE and, unless the tile row in $74AA is 9, the bottom pair from $915C to the row below; then moves the pointer on 2 characters. Keeps X and Y in the operands at $74E5 and $74E7. Called by $7337.
Holds the X register saved by $74AB: the immediate operand of the LDX at $74E4.
Holds the Y register saved by $74B1: the immediate operand of the LDY at $74E6.

Writes only the right half of tile A at the screen pointer $ED/$EE: the top right character from $90BF and, unless the tile row in $74AA is 9, the bottom right character from $915D to the row below; then moves the pointer on 1 character. Keeps X and Y in the operands at $7517 and $7519. Used by $7337 for the first tile of each row.
Holds the X register saved by $74E9: the immediate operand of the LDX at $7516.
Holds the Y register saved by $74EF: the immediate operand of the LDY at $7518.

Tests whether a slot in state 7 (the follower behaviour $1C47) stands in the player's way to the left. Returns A=0 at once when the resident flag $0A10 is non-zero. Otherwise it goes through slots $0A down to 0 in state 7 whose previous object's slot is not in state $10 and returns A=1 when the slot's screen X $87,X (high byte $BF,X zero) is at or up to $13 left of the player's $1D80 and the player's $1D81 is at most $13 lines below, or $27 lines above, the slot's height $A3,X minus $15 ($52F4); A=0 if no slot is. Called by the player states ($5A2A, $5B7B, $5D2D, $5E88) before a step left.
A lone RTS right after the jump at $7558 in blocked_left: no branch, jump or call reaches it.

Second part of blocked_left ($751B). Reached by the branch at $754E when the player's height $1D81 is below the follower's height minus $15 (kept in $52F4): it gives up unless the follower is less than $28 lines below the player. From $7567, which the first part also reaches, the follower counts only when its screen X high byte $BF is 0 and its screen X $87 is the player's $1D80 or less than $14 below it; it returns A=1 then and otherwise goes back to the slot loop at $7529.

The same test as $751B for a step to the right: returns A=1 when a slot in state 7 has its screen X at or up to $13 right of the player's $1D80 (same height test), otherwise A=0. Called by the player states ($5A4C, $5BC3, $5D5B, $5EB6) before a step right.
A lone RTS right after the jump at $75C1 in blocked_right: no branch, jump or call reaches it.

Second part of blocked_right ($7584). Reached by the branch at $75B7 when the player's height $1D81 is below the follower's height minus $15 (kept in $52F4): it gives up unless the follower is less than $28 lines below the player. From $75D0, which the first part also reaches, the follower counts only when its screen X high byte $BF is 0 and its screen X $87 is the player's $1D80 or more than the player's by less than $14 (it returns A=1 then); otherwise it goes back to the slot loop at $7592.

Called by the top interrupt at $646D while the banner flag $771A is set. Turns on all eight sprites as multicolour with colour $0F (multicolours 1 and $0B, no expansion), sets their X positions ($87, $9F, $B7 and $CF, in two rows of four) and busy-waits on the raster until line $96: below line $62 it sets heights $3C and $51 and the pointers $C5-$CC through $76C7, and from line $62 to $91 it moves sprites 0-3 to height $66, sets the pointers $CD-$D4 and puts sprites 4-7 at height $7B, 21 lines below. It sets the border to black before returning. Probably draws a large picture across the screen.
Sets the heights of sprites 0-3 to A and of sprites 4-7 to A plus $15, then falls into $76E2.
Sets the eight sprite pointers in both screens' tables ($CFF8-$CFFF and $CBF8-$CBFF) to X, X+1, up to X+7.

1 while the banner at $75EE is on; set by the behaviour $122C (at $124A), cleared by the setup and by $771E at the end. The top interrupt $6428, the bottom interrupt $638F (which then skips the scroll step $1ECD) and $771E read it.
Time left of the banner, counted down by $771E on each pass of the main loop; set to $C8 by the behaviour $122C (at $124F), which starts it, and cleared by the setup.
Set to 1 by $771E once the banner has run; the banner step does nothing after that.
The RTS that the early exits of banner_step ($771E) branch to, just before it.

Called by the main loop at $1E27. Returns at once when $771C is set or the banner flag $771A is clear. When the timer $771B holds $C8 it blacks the colour RAM of the playfield ($D800-$DAF7); it counts $771B down and when it reaches 1 puts the colours back from the screen matrix on show ($1EC8 picks $C800 or $CC00) through the table at $BF00, sets $771C and clears $771A. The behaviour $122C sets $771A and $771B.
The four masks $FC, $F0, $C0 and $00 that $7803 uses to take pixels off the end of the energy bar.
64 bytes of shapes for the eight characters of the energy bar, built by $7803 and copied to $FAC8.
Counter of $7803: starts at the energy $5366 and counts up to $21 as the bar's pixels are masked off.

Builds the energy bar: fills 8 cells of the panel's screen matrix ($CF59 on) with the colours $1D and their colour RAM ($DB59) with 5, writes a striped pattern into the eight 8-byte cells at $77C2, masks off one multicolour pixel (two bits) for each step by which the energy $5366 is below $21, from the right-hand end (mask table at $77BE), and copies the 64 bytes at $77C2 to the panel bitmap at $FAC8. Called by the main loop at $1E1E.

Adds A to the decimal digit $0A00+X and carries towards the more significant digits (X counting down), going on down to digit 0 every time and adding a carry of 0 once a digit does not overflow; keeps Y. Digit 6 is the units, so the 4 and 8 added to digit 5 by $615B are 40 and 80 points.
Scratch of $788B: the amount to add, then the carry to the next digit.
Draws the seven digits from $0A00 on into the panel bitmap's cells at $FA58 (8 bytes each, from the digit shapes at $1DC4) through $78CA. Called by the main loop at $1E2A.
Copies the 8-byte shape of digit $0A00+X from $1DC4 to the pointer $85/$86 and moves the pointer on 8 bytes; keeps X. Called seven times by $78B7.
The 73 starting types of the objects, copied to $0AA2 by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 starting counters, copied to $0AEB by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 starting flags, copied to $0B34 by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 starting energy, copied to $0B7D by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 variant flags, copied to $0BC6 by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 starting values of the second flag, copied to $0C0F by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 left limits of the walks, low bytes, copied to $0C58 by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 left limits of the walks, high bytes, copied to $0CA1 by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 right limits of the walks, low bytes, copied to $0CEA by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 right limits of the walks, high bytes, copied to $0D33 by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 starting world X, low bytes, copied to $0D7C by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 starting world X, high bytes, copied to $0DC5 by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 starting world Y, low bytes, copied to $0E0E by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).
The 73 starting world Y, high bytes, copied to $0E57 by $73C2 (the 14 tables from $78F0 to $7CED are 73 bytes apart).

The level map: 72 rows of 64 tile numbers (0 to 61), row r at $7CEE + 64 x r (pointers in map_row_pointers). A tile number picks two characters of the top row from tile_top_chars ($90BE) and two of the bottom row from tile_bottom_chars ($915C), which $7337 and the scroll routines draw two by two. Column 0 is tile $0C in 68 rows, column 1 is $08 in 61, column 58 is $08 in 66 and columns 60 to 63 are $0C in 67; rows 70 and 71 are all tile 5. This symbol covers the map from row 0 column 0 ($7CEE) to row 12 column 17 ($7FFF): of its 786 numbers, tile $15 296, tile $0C 129, tile $00 68.
The level map, from row 12 column 18 ($8000) to row 28 column 17 ($83FF) (a symbol reaches at most to a $8000 edge or 1,024 bytes): of its 1,024 numbers, tile $15 225, tile $00 107, tile $0C 96.
The level map, from row 28 column 18 ($8400) to row 44 column 17 ($87FF): of its 1,024 numbers, tile $15 338, tile $00 115, tile $05 112.
The level map, from row 44 column 18 ($8800) to row 60 column 17 ($8BFF): of its 1,024 numbers, tile $15 265, tile $00 113, tile $0C 96.
The level map, from row 60 column 18 ($8C00) to row 71 column 63 ($8EED): of its 750 numbers, tile $15 194, tile $05 134, tile $01 70.
Two bytes of $7F after the last map row, the pair that also ends each of the three paths that follow. No code addresses them.

Path 0 of behaviour $5398 (variant 0), 154 bytes: 76 pairs of signed bytes, the X offset and then the Y offset from the object's anchor, one pair a frame, ended by $7F, $7F. Both offsets run from -12 to +13, a loop round the anchor.

Path 1 of behaviour $5398 (variant 1), 154 bytes: 76 pairs of signed bytes, the X offset and then the Y offset from the object's anchor, ended by $7F, $7F. The X offsets run from -24 to +25 and the Y offsets from -25 to +24, a loop round the anchor.

Path 2 of behaviour $5398 (variant 2), 154 bytes: 76 pairs of signed bytes, the X offset and then the Y offset from the object's anchor, ended by $7F, $7F. The X offsets run from -36 to +37 and the Y offsets from -37 to +35, a loop round the anchor.

For each tile (index times 2) the two screen codes of its top row; the characters count in strips of 40 across the character set. Read by draw_tile ($74AB), draw_tile_right_half ($74E9), the column routines draw_right_column ($2164) and draw_left_column ($34BA), and the row routines $26B7, $27A6, $2A52 and $2B38 through their self-modified operands. The extent is the pattern up to the text at $913A.

34 bytes in screen codes after tile_top_chars that nothing reads: "TRACK  AND  DARKMAN  IS", $FF, " CORNERED " (letters as 1 to 26, doubled spaces as in the briefing), with no closing $FF. The table tile_bottom_chars starts right after it.

For each tile (index times 2) the two screen codes of its bottom row, read by draw_tile ($74AB), draw_tile_right_half ($74E9), the column routines $2164 and $34BA, and the row routines $26B7, $27A6, $2A52 and $2B38 through their self-modified operands. The extent is the pattern up to the panel bytes at $91DC.

The 200 screen-matrix bytes of the status panel, copied to $CEF7 by $52C4. The panel is shown in multicolour bitmap mode, so each byte holds a cell's two colours, not a screen code. $CEF7 is row 18 column 39, so the first byte lands in the playfield and panel rows 19 to 23 take bytes 1 to 199.
The 200 colours of the status panel, copied to colour RAM $DAF7 by $52C4.
Lengths of the 56 diagonal lines of the wipe in $93AB, each one less than the number of characters the line clears: $93AB stores a character before it tests the count for zero.
The last two entries (1 and 0) of wipe_lengths: the wipe $93AB stops at line $38 (56), so it never reads them.
Characters still to clear on the diagonal line $93AB is drawing, after the one just stored: loaded from $936C and counted down until it is zero, so a line clears one more character than its entry.
Low byte of the screen address where the current diagonal line of $93AB starts. After each of lines 0 to 38 the start moves one character right, and after the later lines 40 characters, one row down.
High byte of the screen address where the current diagonal line of $93AB starts ($CC at the first line).
Set to 1 by $93AB and cleared by the setup; while it is set the top interrupt $6428 does not turn the sprites on.

Wipes the screen: sets the wipe flag $93A9 and the pause flag $63EA, then clears both screen matrices ($CC00 and $C800) in 56 diagonal lines, each stepping 39 characters from its start with the lengths taken from $936C, a delay through $6534 after each, and clears the pause flag at the end. The first 40 lines start along the top row (columns 0 to 39), the last 16 down the right edge. Called by the main loop before it leaves the level, by the game over screen and when the NMI ends the level.
Holds the line index saved by $93F8: the immediate operand of the LDX at $9403.
Holds the Y register saved by $93FB: the immediate operand of the LDY at $9405.
The three digits of the countdown timer, $9449 the units to $944B the hundreds; set at the start to 500 when $0A10 is set.
The countdown timer's tens digit (0 to 9), the middle one of the three timer digits; counted down by $948A when the units digit wraps from 0 to 9.
The countdown timer's hundreds digit; counted down by $948A when the tens digit wraps. The timer starts at 500 when $0A10 is set.
Draws the three timer digits into the panel's character shapes at $F9D8 (hundreds, $944B), $F9E8 (tens, $944A) and $F9F0 (units, $9449) through $9474. Called by the main loop at $1E2D.
Copies the 8-byte shape of the timer digit $9449+X from $1DC4 to the pointer $85/$86. Called three times by $944C.
Alternates 1 and 0 on each call of $948A that gets past its tests (not paused, digits not all zero); $948A counts the timer down only when it finds 0.

Called by the middle interrupt $62BF at $6366 every frame; does nothing while the game is paused ($63EA). When the three timer digits $9449-$944B are zero it clears $0A10 and sets the timer state $94FD to 1; otherwise on every second call ($9489 alternates 1 and 0) it counts the digits down by one, the units first.
Called by the main loop at $1E30. When the timer state $94FD is 1 it sets it to 2 and runs $9567, which replaces the timer's picture in the panel; in any other state it does nothing.

Set to 1 by $948A on every frame (while not paused) that the timer digits read 000; $94EC then steps it to 2 and redraws the panel graphics, so once the timer is at zero this repeats on every pass of the main loop, from the start of the level when $0A10 was clear. Nothing sets it to 0.

Copies a picture of 6 by 5 characters into the panel: the shapes (48 bytes each from $96FC, $972C, $975C, $978C and $97BC to $F8C0, $FA00, $FB40, $FC80 and $FDC0), the colours (6 bytes each from $97EC-$9804 to $DB18-$DBB8) and the screen codes (from $980A-$9822 to $CF18-$CFB8). Drawn by $52C4 while $0A10 is set.

The same copy as $94FE from the other set of data ($95D0-$96FB): the shapes from $95D0, $9600, $9630, $9660 and $9690, the colours from $96C0-$96D8 and the screen codes from $96DE-$96F6. Drawn by $52C4 when $0A10 is clear, and by $94EC once the timer is at zero, again on every pass of the main loop after that.

The set of data $9567 copies into the panel: 5 rows of 48 bytes of shapes, then 5 rows of 6 colours ($96C0) and 5 rows of 6 screen codes ($96DE). The picture drawn when $0A10 is clear or the timer has run out.
The set of data $94FE copies into the panel: 5 rows of 48 bytes of shapes, then 5 rows of 6 colours ($97EC) and 5 rows of 6 screen codes ($980A). The picture drawn while $0A10 is set.

Writes the continue screen's texts "PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE" from $9875 at $CD49 and "CREDITS" from $988C at $CF8C, adding $66 to each code and turning $20 into 0 (each ends at $FF), then the digit of $0A12 at $CF94 and the digit of $9873 at $CE1C (both as $8A plus the digit). Called by $98A4.
The countdown shown on the continue screen, from 9; counted down by $98A4 and drawn by $9828.
Set to 1 by $9B76 when the briefing has ended; nothing else in the traced code reads it.
"PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE" in screen codes, ended by $FF; written by $9828.
"CREDITS" followed by spaces in screen codes, ended by $FF; written by $9828, with the digit of $0A12 after it.
Set to 1 by $98A4 when fire is pressed to continue; read by the main loop at $1E57.

The continue screen, entered from the main loop at $1E54 when the energy is zero, the cheat flag $0A11 is clear and $0A12 (the credits) is not zero, after the game over screen $57FF. Sets up the text screen, clears the score digits $0A00-$0A06 and $0A10, swaps the shapes ($9B3B), draws the texts through $9828 and counts $9873 down from 9 with delays; fire (bit 4 of $DC00) takes one from $0A12 and sets the continue flag $98A3 to 1, and when the count runs out the flag stays 0. Then puts the shapes back and redraws the panel ($52C4).
136 bytes of character shapes that $9B3B swaps with the block at $C338.
136 bytes of character shapes that $9B3B swaps with the block at $C3C0.
Key code read by $9A81 and stored by $1F88; $50 pauses ($739B), $20 can end the level (main loop at $1E3E).

Reads the keyboard with CIA 1 into A. Returns $FF at once when any of the low five bits of $DC00 AND $DC01 reads low (the test at $9A8C, so while the joystick or a key in that range is down); otherwise scans the eight rows from $9AF8, looks the key up in the table at $9AFB and returns its code (also keeping the table index in $02A7). $1F88 keeps the result in $9A80.
The row select value written to $DC00 by $9A81 while it scans the keyboard, rotated one bit for each row.
The number of the keyboard row $9A81 is scanning.

The column bits read from $DC01 for the row being scanned by $9A81, kept after they have been shifted right past the key just found, so that the scan can go on through the rest of the row when that key has no code.
Key codes for the 64 keys of the matrix, indexed by 8 times the column plus the row; $80 and above mean no code. Read by $9A81.

Exchanges three blocks: 136 bytes at $9948 and 136 at $99D0 with $C338 and $C3C0, and the 80 bytes of digit shapes at $1DC4 with $C450. Called to put the text screens' shapes in and to restore the play shapes.

Counts the passes of the typing loop of $9B76 down from $1E; fire is not tested until it reaches 0. A line end takes a pass as a character does, so fire is first tested after 29 characters and the first line end.
Index of the next character of the briefing text at $9C0A for $9B76.

Types the level briefing from $9C0A on the screen one character at a time, from $CC56, with a delay through $6534 before each: adds $66 to each code (a space becomes 0), $FF ends a line (the pointer moves on 2 rows) and a second $FF ends the text, which then waits for fire (bit 4 of $DC00). Fire is ignored for the first 30 passes of the loop ($9B74), which are 29 characters and the first line end; pressing it later skips to the end, where $9874 is set to 1 and two long delays run. It first waits, clears the screen and fills colour RAM with 7; the setup calls $9B3B before and after it.
Holds the Y register saved by $9BAC: the immediate operand of the LDY at $9BB4.

The level briefing in screen codes (A is 1, a space is $20, a full stop is $1B), lines ended by $FF and the text by a second $FF; it reads "LEVEL FOUR. DESCENDING TO HIS LAB DARKMAN MUST OPEN THE GAS CYLINDERS THEN SET THE BIRD ROCKING OVER THE LIGHTER AND ESCAPE BACK UP TO THE ROOFTOP. THE DOOM INTENDED FOR HIM SHALL NOW BEFALL HIS ENEMIES. END OF LINE...". Typed by $9B76.
254 bytes after the briefing text, to the end of the level file at $9DFF: mostly $FF and $00 with other values scattered between. No code reads them.

Colour for each character code, indexed by the character; the colour buffer routines $3867 and $44BF (and their continuation parts), fill_colour_top ($6FF4), $7337 and $771E read it to fill the colour RAM, and the setup $5118 ORs $08 into every entry.
Pointer $00: 64 zero bytes, the empty frame. The text screens read their character set from $C000 ($D018=$30 in the setup $5118), so these bytes are also character 0, the blank.

Sprite shapes for pointers $01 to $0B and the first 56 bytes of $0C (760 bytes). In use: $01 in the frame table $5723 (behaviour $573B); $02 and $03, an enemy walking right of variant 0 (table $189B); $05 and $06, walking left (table $1651); $04 and $07, the frames at counter $0E of the attacks $17A9 and $155E for variant 0; $08 to $0B, the frames of slot_follow below its limit (table $1CE3); $0C, with $0D to $0F, the frames of slot_follow at or above its limit (table $1CC3).

136 bytes that $9B3B swaps with text_shapes_a ($9948). On the text screens they are character shapes of the font; during play they are sprite data, the last 8 bytes of pointer $0C and all of $0D and $0E, which slot_follow shows through follow_frames_high ($1CC3).

136 bytes that $9B3B swaps with text_shapes_b ($99D0). On the text screens they are character shapes of the font; during play they are sprite data: all of pointer $0F (follow_frames_high), all of $10 and the first 8 bytes of $11, the frames of an enemy of variant 1 walking right (table $18BB).

8 bytes between the swapped letters (char_shapes_text_b) and the swapped digits (char_shapes_digits): the font's character 137, which $9B3B leaves alone. During play they are bytes 8 to 15 of the sprite shape for pointer $11.
80 bytes that $9B3B swaps with the digit shapes at $1DC4. On the text screens they are the font's digits; during play they are sprite data, bytes 16 to 63 of pointer $11 and bytes 0 to 31 of $12.

Sprite shapes from byte 32 of pointer $12 to the end of $1F (864 bytes). In use: $12 and $13 and $16 and $17, the attack frames of variant 1 ($17A9 and $155E); $14 and $15, walking left of variant 1 (table $1671); $18 (variant 0) and $1C (variant 1), the shapes of the knocked-down frames of $6222; $19 to $1C and $1D and $1E, the frames of follow_frames_a and follow_frames_b; $1F in the frame table $5723.

Screen matrix A: 25 rows of 40 characters in text mode, of which the playfield uses the first 19; written by the scroll routines and the row routines draw_top_row_b ($2B38) and draw_bottom_row_b ($27A6). $D018 selects it, or screen_b, from screen_buffer ($1EC8) through $62A9; the panel rows always come from screen_b.

The sprite pointers of screen A's table ($CBF8-$CBFF); the player's sprites 0 to 2 are written by $60C0, sprites 3 to 7 by the multiplexer $6593, sprite 3 also by the top interrupt $6428, and the banner's by $75EE and $76E2; the middle interrupt $62BF sets all eight to 0 every frame. Always written together with sprite_pointers_b.
Screen matrix B: the same layout as screen_a, 25 rows of 40 characters. The briefing is typed into it at $CC56 and the game over text at $CD50; the panel is drawn into it by $52C4.

The sprite pointers of screen B's table ($CFF8-$CFFF); the player's sprites 0 to 2 are written by $60C0, sprites 3 to 7 by the multiplexer $6593, sprite 3 also by the top interrupt $6428, and the banner's by $75EE and $76E2; the middle interrupt $62BF sets all eight to 0 every frame. These also write sprite_pointers_a; fill_screen ($656D) clears this table alone when it fills screen B for the text screens.

Characters 0 to 127 of level 4's play character set (1,024 bytes, 8 bytes a character, one byte a pixel row). The top interrupt irq_top ($6428) stores $34 in $D018 at $644E, which sets the character base to $D000 and the screen to $CC00; select_screen ($62A9) then switches the screen between $CC00 and $C800 and keeps the character bits. tile_top_chars ($90BE) and tile_bottom_chars ($915C) pick the codes, and char_colours ($BF00) gives each its colour. Level 6 has a different character set here (1,823 of the 2,048 bytes differ). Only the VIC sees these bytes: with the I/O area switched in, the CPU reads the chips' registers at the same addresses.

Characters 128 to 247 of the play character set (960 bytes), the same form as play_charset_a. The tile tables reach $F3 (tile_top_chars) and $FB (tile_bottom_chars), but the codes $F8 to $FB belong to tiles 62 and 63, which the map does not use, so the map puts codes up to $F7 on the screen; $F8 and up are the blank characters of play_charset_blank. Only the VIC sees these bytes: with the I/O area switched in, the CPU reads the chips' registers at the same addresses.

Characters 248 to 255 (64 bytes), all zero: the blank characters. Sprite pointer $5F would read the same bytes, and pointers $5A to $5E read other characters as sprite data, so $5A to $5F are not shapes.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $60 and $61 (128 bytes): behave_countdown_light ($1262) shows $61 for phases 7 and up and $60 below, single-colour. Read as multicolour they are scattered strokes, so the picture is not clear. Same bytes as in level 6, where no table names them.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $62 and $63 (128 bytes): the pickup of the behaviour at $1A00, named by pickup_frames ($19F2). A heart, in two versions of the same size that differ in their outline colours.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $64 to $66 (192 bytes): three frames of the burst that lobbed_shot_steps ($1BDA) and behave_falling_burst ($57A6) run through, growing from the base like a flame.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shape for pointer $67 (64 bytes): a small ring, the shot picture of behave_radial_shot ($13EF), behave_lobbed_shot ($1B20), behave_path_follower ($5398) and behave_fixed_sprite ($54B3).

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $68 and $69 (128 bytes): the two frames of the patrolling object of behaviour $134D, named by vpatrol_frames ($133E). A wide figure in two poses.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $6A and $6B (128 bytes): behave_flash_frame ($1B00) shows $6B while the object's counter runs and $6A otherwise. Two small figures of the same outline, a wide band that narrows to a point at the bottom.
Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shape for pointer $6C (64 bytes): the pickup of behave_score_pickup ($1ABE), a round body with a letter P drawn on it in a second colour.
Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $6D to $6F (192 bytes): rows of vertical bars at three heights, the flashing hazard of behaviour $14F2, named by flash_frames ($1496).
Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shape for pointer $70 (64 bytes): the tall bar that behave_countdown_start ($122C) gives its slot.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $71 and $72 (128 bytes): the first and last frames of the burst in lobbed_shot_steps ($1BDA), after the three frames of burst_shapes; $72 is mostly empty.
Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $73 and $74 (128 bytes): the shot of behave_enemy_shot ($1295), $73 when it flies right and $74 when it flies left. A small ring.
Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shape for pointer $75 (64 bytes): the round body of behave_bouncer ($5672).

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $76 to $7A (320 bytes): the five frames of the blast that moves left, named by blast_frames_left ($54C3). Read as multicolour they do not show a clear picture.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $7B to $7F (320 bytes): the five frames of the blast that moves right, named by blast_frames_right ($54FC). lobbed_shot_steps ($1BDA) also lists $7B and $7C. Read as multicolour they do not show a clear picture.

Sprite shapes for pointers $80 to $8F (1,024 bytes). Level 4's player_draw ($60C0) writes the pointers into the tables at $CFF8 and $CBF8; of these, $80 to $8B are sprite 2 ($CFFA) of the standing and walking player (F - $17 with F from walk_frames_right ($58F6) or walk_frames_left ($58E4)), and strike_frames ($5996, $59A6) puts $8C and $8D in frame_sprite_2 ($60BD). $8E and $8F have no traced use. The same bytes as level 2's player_shapes_a.

Sprite shapes for pointers $90 to $93 (256 bytes), part of the player's punch and crouch frames: $60BD takes $90 and $91 from punch_frames ($594D) and $92 and $93 from crouch_frames ($5B27). The same bytes as level 2's player_shapes_b.

Sprite shapes for pointers $94 to $96 (192 bytes): the player climbing, picked by climb_frames_up ($5F43) and climb_frames_down ($5F4F). player_draw ($60C0) adds $24 and $2E to each pointer here for the other two climbing sprites ($B8 to $BA and $C2 to $C4). The same bytes as level 2's climb_shapes.

Sprite shapes for pointers $97 to $9C (384 bytes): the player walking right (walk_frames_right at $58F6). player_draw ($60C0) subtracts $17 and adds $0D to each pointer for the other two sprites ($80 to $85 and $A4 to $A9). The same bytes as level 2's walk_right_shapes.

Sprite shapes for pointers $9D to $A2 (384 bytes): the player walking left (walk_frames_left at $58E4), drawn like walk_right_shapes, with $AA to $AF and $86 to $8B as the other two sprites. The same bytes as level 2's walk_left_shapes.

Sprite shapes for pointers $A3 to $B2 (1,024 bytes). player_draw ($60C0) reads $A4 to $AF here as sprite 1 ($CFF9) of the walking player (F + $0D); the punch and crouch frames take $B4 to $B7 from here, and the strike frames $A3 and $B1 (sprite 0) and $B0 (sprite 1). The same bytes as level 2's attack_shapes.

Sprite shapes for pointers $B3 to $C1 (960 bytes), the rest of attack_shapes: $B4 to $B7 are named there, $BB is a strike frame (strike_frames at $59B0), and $B8 to $BA are the second sprite of the player climbing (F + $24, see climb_shapes). The punch and crouch frames put $B4 to $B7 in the operand $60BE and $BE to $C1 in $60BF. The same bytes as level 2's attack_shapes_b.
Sprite shapes for pointers $C2 to $C4 (192 bytes): the third sprite of the player climbing (F + $2E, see climb_shapes). The same bytes as level 2's climb_shapes_c.
Sprite shapes for pointers $C5 to $D4 (1,024 bytes): the banner picture of banner_sprites ($75EE), which sets eight sprite pointers from $C5 and eight from $CD.

Sprite shapes for pointers $D5 to $DA (384 bytes): the player jumping, $D5 (facing right) or $D6 from jump_frame ($5F2F), with sprites 0 and 1 taking that plus 2 and plus 4 ($D7 and $D9, or $D8 and $DA).
Sprite shapes for pointers $DB and $DC (128 bytes), used by behaviour $573B: $DB in its frame table $5723 and $DC as its pointer.
Sprite shapes for pointers $DD and $DE (128 bytes): all zero.

The status panel's bitmap, which the raster interrupt irq_bottom switches on from line $CD (bitmap mode at $E000, multicolour): 40 cells wide, rows 19 to 24, 8 bytes a cell and 320 a row. Level 4's draw_panel ($52C4) copies the picture in (through $94FE or $9567, which timer_expired ($94EC) also calls), draw_timer ($944C) writes the timer digits, draw_score ($78B7) the score digits at $FA58 and draw_bar ($7803) the energy bar at $FAC8. The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap.

Row 19, columns 32 to 37: the first of five rows of the 6 by 5 cell picture that timer_graphics_on ($94FE) or timer_graphics_off ($9567) copies in (48 bytes a row; the others are panel_picture_1 to 4). The same bytes as level 2's panel_picture_0.
Row 19, columns 38 and 39, and row 20, columns 0 to 26: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (232 bytes). The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_1.
